newsitem.title: GREECE: Banks, industrials pull Greek stocks higher at open.
newsitem.headline: Banks, industrials pull Greek stocks higher at open.

text.p: Banks and industrials pulled Greek shares strongly on the upside in early Monday trade and the benchmark index gained 0.79 percent after 25 minutes of trading.
"The stock market has shown signs of rational activity with investors rewarding companies with strong profit growth," said Costas Panagidis, general manager at Axon Securities.
National Bank and Alpha Credit Bank were upbeat, carrying over the tone from the previous week when they announced strong earnings growth in their interim results.
"Reports of the government's intentions for a step up in the role of the capital market in its privatisation programme is also fueling optimism," said Panagidis.
"Investors will be happy to see new arrivals of profitable companies at the stock market and the government will have every reason to keep them happy to buy into the new issues," he added.

Weekend financial press echoed recent reports suggesting that the government had short-listed 10 profitable utilities and other companies which would seek a listing in the near future, starting with oil refinery DEP in late 1997.
The market should be expected to move higher in August but trading volume will limit overall gains as a large number of investors are not in the market at the moment, he added.
"Rising prices have not been accompanied by an increase in turnover," Panagidis said. "Banks will outperform the market with OTE telecom and other blue chip industrials following suit next month."
The Athens general index was up 0.79 percent or 12.59 points at 1,613.98 from Friday's 1,601.39 close after 25 minutes of trading.
Banks and industrials were 0.97 and 0.77 percent higher, respectively.
Turnover was 2.2 billion drachmas on volume of 0.6 million shares.
Advancers led decliners 96 to 27 with 16 shares unchanged on 139 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,123-1,153 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,097-1,157 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying stock were up 5 drachmas at 6,385.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 652.61-694.27 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $74.16-$77.00. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,714-3,940 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $13.05 bid/no offer. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 250-283 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
